clue.text: Forceful detectives holding crowd back

indicators.note: back tells us the whole assembled group of letters is then read from right to left
the clue words that say one part holds the other

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detectives of a British police force
a crowd is many people, so many stands for it

explanation.surface: Tough police officers keep a mob from advancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the crowd between the I and D of the detectives, and 'back' then reverses the lot. CID is the British plain-clothes police branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamic person is energetic and vigorous, as a forceful one is.

clue.text: Animal controller's club

definitions.meaning: someone who drives cattle or sheep to market controls the animals; the 's stands for is
a golf club used for long tee shots

explanation.definitionFit: A drover who herds livestock is a driver, and the golfer's longest wooden club is also called a driver.

clue.text: Unsophisticated old city in African province

indicators.note: in says the old city's letters sit inside the province's name

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city of Abraham, the crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: A traveller describes a simple ancient settlement in southern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone natural is artless and unaffected, without worldly polish.

clue.text: Appropriate solution when a fresh trap's required

definitions.text: Appropriate solution when a fresh trap's required

parts.words: Appropriate solution when a fresh trap's required
parts.note: trap is slang for the mouth and a solution is a liquid, so this is a rinse for freshening the breath, not a puzzle answer or a new snare

explanation.definitionFit: A mouth rinse is a liquid solution used to make the breath fresh.

clue.text: Dramatic film-one depending on a bluff?

definitions.meaning: a suspenseful film or serial episode that leaves the audience in suspense
a bluff is a steep cliff, and depending means hanging, so this is someone dangling from a cliff edge

explanation.definitionFit: A suspense story that ends at a crisis is named after heroes left dangling from a precipice.

clue.text: Husband swimming near ship — it hangs about the bay

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of near are moving about in the water

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A man goes for a swim close to a vessel moored in the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges NEAR into ARNE. The bay is not a stretch of coast but a reddish-brown horse, which wears the tack.
explanation.definitionFit: The straps and fittings of harness are hung round a horse, and a bay is a horse of that colour.

clue.text: Tool the governor carries round

indicators.note: carries means the governor's letters hold the round letter within them

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An official holds a gardening implement as he makes his rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoe is a garden implement for weeding and loosening soil.

clue.text: Right to go on every part of river

indicators.note: to go on means the right letter goes ahead and every follows on after it

parts.note: each and every mean the same here

explanation.surface: A walker claims a right of way along every stretch of the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A reach is a straight stretch of a river between two bends.

clue.text: Becoming horizontal as day's ending

definitions.meaning: the close of the day, after the afternoon

explanation.definitionFit: Levelling a surface is making it even, and the close of the day is also called the evening.

clue.text: Clergyman's producing piece of pottery with it inside

indicators.note: inside says the fashionable word is placed within the pottery fragment

parts.note: a sherd (or shard) is a broken fragment of pottery
hep is old slang for fashionable or with it

explanation.surface: A vicar's hobby is making pots, and he hides a piece in one.
explanation.walkthrough: HEP is dated slang, and a pastor is called a shepherd because he tends his flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor tending his congregation is called its shepherd, a long-standing image for a priest.

clue.text: Confusing sin with virtue can be disturbing

indicators.note: Confusing tells us to jumble the letters that follow into a new order

explanation.surface: Mixing up wickedness with goodness can be upsetting to the moral mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confusing' rearranges the nine letters of SIN and VIRTUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrusive disturbs by forcing itself in where it is not welcome.

clue.text: Murder victim found beside root of elm tree

parts.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, the first murder victim

indicators.note: root of picks the first letter, as a root is where a tree begins

explanation.surface: A body is discovered next to the base of an elm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'root of' takes E, the first letter of 'elm'. An abele is the white poplar.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is another name for the white poplar, a tree.

clue.text: Some tear this, making a hole

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people rip this, leaving a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'making a hole' is changed to 'a hole': the word does not mean digging, it is a fox's hole, and 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's burrow is called its earth, a hole in the ground where it lives.

clue.text: Immediately caught leaving charming woman by river

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river flowing into the Firth of Forth

indicators.note: leaving means the caught letter departs from the charming woman's word

parts.note: a witch casts charms, so she is a charming woman in the magical sense
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Without delay, a man is caught walking out on a delightful woman by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes C out of WITCH to give WITH. 'charming' looks like delightful but means casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthwith means at once, without any delay.

clue.text: Fearful increase includes bill

indicators.note: includes says the bill's letters are taken into the increase word

parts.note: to redouble is to increase, especially effort
a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

explanation.surface: A frightening rise in prices shows up on the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fearful' here means causing fear, not feeling it; a redoubtable opponent is one to be feared.
explanation.definitionFit: Redoubtable means formidable, inspiring fear or awe.

clue.text: Description of intriguing garment with ragged pieces

parts.note: a cloak is a garment
and means with or together with

indicators.note: pieces suggests the word ragged is broken into bits and reassembled

explanation.surface: A tattered coat is described as fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' rearranges RAGGED to DAGGER. 'intriguing' means plotting, not fascinating.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying and secret plotting are described as cloak-and-dagger activities.

clue.text: A new number has a story cut before delivery takes place

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: cut means the story's word is shortened by losing its final letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A fresh issue of a magazine carries a shortened tale before it is delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the story. The delivery is a birth, not a postal round.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal care happens before birth, the delivery of a baby.

clue.text: Angered? That's about right, it appears to be annoying

indicators.note: about says the angered word goes round the following letters

parts.note: irate means angry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are angry and is told that seems fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts right and it inside the angry word, after its first two letters; the question mark makes 'Angered' look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate is to annoy or vex, so it means be annoying to someone.

clue.text: Take steps as quickly as possibly to limit damage done by strikers

definitions.text: Take steps as quickly as possibly to limit damage done by strikers

parts.words: Take steps as quickly as possibly to limit damage done by strikers
parts.note: the strikers are not workers on strike but people hitting you as you hurry between two lines of them, an old punishment

explanation.definitionFit: Running between two rows of men who strike at you is the old punishment behind the phrase for facing hostile criticism.

clue.text: This country's invested in bags with oriental ornament from Japan

indicators.note: invested in says the country's letters are placed inside the others

parts.note: nets are bags made of mesh
E for eastern, oriental
the Times is a British paper, so this country is the UK; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Britain puts money into an eastern ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' looks financial but just means placed inside. The Times speaks of Britain as this country.
explanation.definitionFit: A netsuke is a small carved toggle worn with Japanese traditional dress.

clue.text: Embrace son in strange new place

indicators.note: in says the son's letter sits inside the jumbled letters
strange says the following letters are put in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A parent hugs a son in an unfamiliar new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges N and PLACE into ENCLAP, and S goes in after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclasp is to hold in a clasp or arms, to embrace.

clue.text: Herb proved effective in opening spell

definitions.meaning: a plant grown for its seeds, used in cooking
in the tale of Ali Baba the magic words that opened the robbers' cave began 'Open'

explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is an oil-seed plant, and 'Open sesame' was the password that unsealed the cave in Ali Baba.

clue.text: Explain meaning of popular palindrome

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
the setter lets the word stand for a seven-letter string that reads the same forwards and backwards, here the rest of the answer after the popular piece

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a well-loved palindrome means.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: 'palindrome' supplies no synonym but describes the letters that follow IN, which read identically both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to explain or translate what something means.

clue.text: It provides airlift to take gold over hill

indicators.note: over means the gold letters are turned over, read the other way

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A helicopter is used to fly treasure over a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns OR into RO, which is followed by TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning blade assembly that gives a helicopter its lift.

clue.text: Suitable position for one received with honour in Tyneside

indicators.note: received means the north-eastern letters take the following ones inside them

parts.note: Tyneside, round Newcastle, is in the north-east of England, NE
I is the Roman numeral one
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: A visitor is given a warm welcome and an award in Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' signals a container. Tyneside is the area round Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a place or role that suits someone perfectly.

clue.text: Not a minor form of education

definitions.meaning: someone who is grown up and of full legal age
classes for grown-ups, as in evening classes

explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up past the age of majority is an adult, and teaching for grown-ups is adult education.

clue.text: Start a bus moving around bases

indicators.note: moving around says the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A bus pulls away and drives around military bases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving around' signals an anagram of the first three words; 'bases' is a noun for foundations, not military camps.
explanation.definitionFit: Substrata are underlying layers, the foundations or bases of something.

clue.text: Broadcast thus to an audience

indicators.note: to an audience means the word is spoken and heard rather than read

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A presenter's words go out on air to the listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' means scattering seed by hand, not transmitting a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To sow seed by scattering it widely is to broadcast it.

clue.text: There's a show of disapproval when it's raised on the ridge

definitions.text: There's a show of disapproval when it's raised on the ridge

parts.words: There's a show of disapproval when it's raised on the ridge
parts.note: the ridge is the bony brow above the eye, not a mountain ridge, and raising this hair line shows doubt

explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the hair line above the eye is a facial gesture of surprise or disapproval.

clue.text: Ball knocked about in various directions in the Oval, loosely

indicators.note: in says the reversed ball sits inside the compass letters

parts.note: east, south and east give compass points E, S, E

indicators.note: knocked about says the ball's word is turned round

parts.note: a pill is a small ball, as in old slang for a cricket or tennis ball

explanation.surface: A ball is struck around in all directions at the Oval cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked about' reverses the ball, and 'in' places it inside the compass points. The Oval is a London cricket ground, but here it is the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is a regular oval shape, so loosely an oval.
